name: Shri Palitana Temples
shortDescription: A cluster of over 863 temples on Shatrunjaya Hill, the most sacred Shvetambara Jain pilgrimage.
description: Palitana temples are located on Shatrunjaya Hill near Palitana in Bhavnagar district, Gujarat. There are more than 863 marble-carved temples exquisitely built on the hill, making it one of the largest temple complexes in the world. The main temple is dedicated to Shri Adinath (Rishabhadeva), the first Tirthankara. The climb consists of 3,500 steps and takes 1.5 to 2 hours. Numerous Jain sadhus and sadhvis attained Moksha here, and the city was declared the first vegetarian city in the world in 2014.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Bhavnagar (50 km). Nearest railway station: Palitana (3 km). Well connected by road from Ahmedabad (215 km).
dharamshalaInfo: Multiple dharamshalas at the base (Taleti) managed by various Jain trusts, offering clean rooms and Jain bhojanshala.

name: Shri Dilwara Temples
shortDescription: Famous for stunning marble carvings, these 11th–13th century temples are a masterpiece of Jain architecture.
description: The Dilwara Temples are a group of five Jain temples at Mount Abu, Rajasthan, built between the 11th and 13th centuries by Vimal Shah and Vastupala-Tejapala. They are renowned worldwide for extraordinary marble carvings treated like lace and filigree. The Vimal Vasahi temple (1031 CE) dedicated to Adinath and the Luna Vasahi temple (1230 CE) dedicated to Neminath are the most famous. Despite their plain exterior, the interiors are breathtaking in craftsmanship.
highlights: Five distinct temples in the complex
howToReach: Nearest airport: Udaipur (185 km). Nearest railway station: Abu Road (29 km). Regular buses from Ahmedabad, Udaipur and Jaipur.
dharamshalaInfo: Several Jain dharamshalas available in Mount Abu town, including Shri Adinath Jain Dharamshala.

name: Shri Ranakpur Jain Temple
shortDescription: Famous for 1,444 intricately carved marble pillars, each unique — a marvel of 15th century Jain art.
description: The Ranakpur Jain Temple (Chaturmukha Dharana Vihara) is a white marble temple dedicated to Adinatha in Pali district, Rajasthan. Built in the 15th century, it is famous for 1,444 marble pillars, no two alike. The four-faced Adinath idol in the sanctum gave it the name 'Chaturmukha'. Covering 48,000 sq ft, it was built by Seth Dharna Shah with the support of Rana Kumbha of Mewar. It is one of the five principal Jain pilgrimage destinations.
highlights: One of five principal Jain pilgrimages
howToReach: Nearest airport: Udaipur (96 km). Nearest railway station: Falna (30 km). Well connected by road from Udaipur and Jodhpur.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala run by Anandji Kalyanji Trust near the temple complex with basic accommodation.

name: Shri Shravanabelagola
shortDescription: Home to the magnificent 57-foot monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali (Gommateshwara) carved from a single granite block.
description: Shravanabelagola in Hassan district, Karnataka, is home to the iconic 57-foot monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali (Gommateshwara) atop Vindhyagiri Hill. Carved from a single granite block in 981 CE, it is one of the largest free-standing statues in the world. Every 12 years, the grand Mahamastakabhisheka ceremony anoints the statue with milk, saffron, and sandalwood. The site has been a Jain center since the 3rd century BCE when Chandragupta Maurya is believed to have spent his last days here as a monk.
highlights: Carved from single granite block (981 CE)
howToReach: Nearest airport: Bengaluru (144 km). Nearest railway station: Hassan (50 km). Regular buses from Bengaluru and Mysuru.
dharamshalaInfo: Multiple Jain dharamshalas and mathas at the base of Vindhyagiri hill for pilgrims.

name: Shri Girnar Temples
shortDescription: Sacred mountain with Jain temples at the summit, including the famous Neminath temple at over 3,500 feet.
description: Girnar is a group of mountains in Junagadh, Gujarat, and one of the most important Jain pilgrimage centers. The Jain temples sit on the first peak at around 3,300 feet, requiring a climb of approximately 10,000 steps. The main temple dedicated to the 22nd Tirthankara Neminath marks where he attained Moksha. Dating from the 12th century, these temples showcase exquisite stone carvings. The trek is both a physical and spiritual journey with breathtaking panoramic views.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Rajkot (102 km). Nearest railway station: Junagadh (5 km). Well connected by road from Ahmedabad (327 km).
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshalas available at Girnar Taleti (base) managed by various Jain trusts.

name: Shri Shankheshwar Parshwanath
shortDescription: One of the most revered Jain temples with a miraculous Moolnayak idol of Parshwanath dating back centuries.
description: Shri Shankheshwar Parshwanath Temple is one of the holiest Jain pilgrimage sites, located in Shankheshwar village of Patan district, Gujarat. The temple houses the revered Moolnayak idol of Shri Parshwanath, the 23rd Tirthankara, believed to be Swayambhu (self-manifested). The idol is considered extremely powerful and miraculous. The temple has a rich history spanning over a thousand years with grand architecture and beautiful carvings.
highlights: One of most visited Jain temples
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ahmedabad (130 km). Nearest railway station: Patan (24 km). Well connected by road from Ahmedabad.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala available near the temple managed by Shankheshwar Parshwanath Trust.

name: Shri Sammed Shikharji
shortDescription: The supreme Jain pilgrimage — the hill where 20 of the 24 Tirthankaras attained Moksha.
description: Sammed Shikharji (Parasnath Hill) in Giridih, Jharkhand, at 4,430 feet is the most sacred Jain pilgrimage site. It is believed that 20 out of 24 Tirthankaras attained Moksha here. The yatra involves a 27 km trek around the hill visiting the Tonks (shrines) of each Tirthankara, taking 8-10 hours. Both Shvetambara and Digambara traditions consider this the most important Tirth. The serene environment makes this a profoundly moving spiritual experience.
highlights: Tonks of each Tirthankara along the path
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ranchi (180 km). Nearest railway station: Parasnath (22 km) / Madhuban (10 km). Buses from Ranchi and Kolkata.
dharamshalaInfo: Large dharamshala complexes at Madhuban (base town) managed by multiple Jain trusts with hundreds of rooms.

name: Shri Kundalpur
shortDescription: Believed to be the birthplace of Lord Mahavira — a serene pilgrimage surrounded by hills in Bihar.
description: Kundalpur in Nalanda district, Bihar, is believed by Digambara Jains to be the birthplace of Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara. The site features the Bada Mandir (main temple) atop a hillock with a beautiful idol of Lord Mahavira. There are over 26 Jain temples in and around Kundalpur. The serene atmosphere surrounded by hills provides a peaceful setting for spiritual reflection. Thousands visit during Mahavir Jayanti.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Patna (90 km). Nearest railway station: Rajgir (13 km). Well connected by road from Patna and Nalanda.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain Dharamshala available within the temple complex for pilgrims.

name: Shri Sonagiri
shortDescription: A cluster of 77 exquisite Jain temples on a hilltop, where millions of monks attained Moksha.
description: Sonagiri in Datia district, Madhya Pradesh, is a sacred Jain Siddhakshetra with 77 Jain temples (mostly Digambara) perched atop a hill. It is believed that approximately 5 million Jain monks attained Moksha from this sacred hill. The main temple houses an idol of Lord Chandraprabhu, the 8th Tirthankara. The white-washed temples dotting the hillside present a spectacular sight. The climb is moderate with well-maintained steps.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Gwalior (68 km). Nearest railway station: Sonagir (2 km). Well connected by road from Gwalior and Jhansi.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala at the base with basic rooms managed by Digambar Jain Samaj.

name: Shri Mahavirji Temple
shortDescription: A major Digambara pilgrimage known for its magnificent temple and the grand annual Rath Yatra.
description: Shri Mahavirji Temple is a famous Jain pilgrimage center in Karauli district, Rajasthan, on the banks of the Gambhir river. The temple houses a beautiful idol of Lord Mahavira in Padmasana posture. It is one of the most important Atishaya Kshetras in Jainism. The annual five-day Rath Yatra during Chaitra Shukla attracts hundreds of thousands of devotees. The campus includes a museum, dharamshala, and beautiful gardens.
highlights: On the banks of Gambhir river
howToReach: Nearest airport: Jaipur (155 km). Nearest railway station: Shri Mahavirji (1 km). Regular trains from Jaipur and Delhi.
dharamshalaInfo: Large dharamshala complex within temple campus with modern amenities and Jain bhojanshala.

name: Shri Pawapuri
shortDescription: The sacred land where Lord Mahavira attained Nirvana — home to the iconic Jalmandir (Water Temple).
description: Pawapuri in Nalanda district, Bihar, is one of the holiest Jain sites where Lord Mahavira attained Nirvana around 527 BCE. The main attraction is the Jalmandir, a white marble temple in the middle of a lotus pond. According to tradition, so many people collected Mahavira's funeral ashes that the soil was dug away, creating the pond. The Samosharan temple marks where Mahavira gave his last sermon. Both traditions consider this profoundly significant.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Patna (83 km). Nearest railway station: Rajgir (26 km) / Bihar Sharif (15 km). Regular buses from Patna.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain Dharamshala near Jalmandir with rooms and bhojanshala for pilgrims.

name: Khandagiri & Udayagiri Caves
shortDescription: Ancient rock-cut caves from the 2nd century BCE, built for Jain monks during King Kharavela's reign.
description: The Khandagiri and Udayagiri caves near Bhubaneswar, Odisha, were carved in the 2nd century BCE as residential blocks for Jain monks during King Kharavela's reign. Udayagiri has 18 caves and Khandagiri has 15. The Hathi Gumpha features a famous inscription by King Kharavela detailing his military campaigns and Jain patronage. The Rani Gumpha is the largest and most decorated cave. These represent some of the earliest surviving Jain monuments in India.
howToReach: Located in Bhubaneswar city, 6 km from railway station. Nearest airport: Bhubaneswar (10 km). Auto-rickshaws and cabs available.

name: Shri Taranga Hill
shortDescription: An ancient hilltop pilgrimage with a magnificent 12th century temple dedicated to Shri Ajitanath, the 2nd Tirthankara.
description: Taranga Hill is a renowned Shvetambara Jain pilgrimage located near Mehsana in North Gujarat. The main temple atop the hill is dedicated to Shri Ajitanath, the 2nd Tirthankara, and dates back to the 12th century. Built from sandstone by the Solanki rulers, it features stunning architectural carvings. The climb of about 500 steps through forested terrain makes for a meditative journey. The temple complex also houses smaller shrines and a museum of Jain artifacts. The annual Patotsav festival draws thousands of devotees.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ahmedabad (140 km). Nearest railway station: Mehsana (35 km). Buses and shared autos from Mehsana.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala at the base of the hill managed by Taranga Tirth Pedhi.

name: Shri Mahudi Jain Temple
shortDescription: A highly revered shrine of Shri Ghantakarna Mahavir Dev, famous for wish fulfillment and spiritual protection.
description: Shri Mahudi Jain Temple near Mehsana, Gujarat, is one of the most popular Jain shrines dedicated to Shri Ghantakarna Mahavir Dev. The temple is especially famous for the belief that prayers here for protection and wish fulfillment are readily answered. The deity is depicted wearing bells (ghanta) on his ears (karna), hence the name. The temple sees a continuous stream of devotees throughout the year, with peak footfall on Tuesdays and during Navratri. The complex includes modern facilities, a large prayer hall, and beautiful gardens.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ahmedabad (80 km). Nearest railway station: Mehsana (22 km). Regular buses and shared autos from Mehsana.
dharamshalaInfo: Modern dharamshala with AC/non-AC rooms, bhojanshala, and parking on campus.

name: Shri Kumbharia Jain Temples
shortDescription: A group of five ancient Jain temples near Ambaji with exquisite carvings rivalling Dilwara temples.
description: The Kumbharia Jain Temples are a group of five stunning Jain temples located near Ambaji in the Banaskantha district of Gujarat. Built between the 11th and 13th centuries during the Solanki era, these temples are renowned for their extraordinarily detailed marble and stone carvings. Often compared to the Dilwara temples of Mount Abu, the Kumbharia temples feature intricately carved ceilings, pillars, and doorways. The Neminath temple is the most prominent of the five. Despite being lesser-known, these temples are an architectural treasure of medieval Jain art.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ahmedabad (170 km). Nearest railway station: Ambaji Road (20 km). Buses from Ahmedabad and Palanpur.

name: Shri Idar Jain Temple
shortDescription: A hilltop Jain pilgrimage in North Gujarat with ancient temples and the revered idol of Shri Adinath.
description: Idar is an important Jain pilgrimage site located in the Sabarkantha district of Gujarat. The temples are situated atop a rocky hill, requiring a climb of about 3,000 steps. The main temple is dedicated to Shri Adinath (Rishabhadeva) and houses an ancient idol of great veneration. The hilltop offers panoramic views of the surrounding Aravalli range. The site has references in ancient Jain texts and is considered a Kalyanak Kshetra. The complex includes multiple temples of various Tirthankaras built over centuries.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ahmedabad (100 km). Nearest railway station: Himmatnagar (25 km). Buses from Ahmedabad and Himatnagar.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala at the base of the hill with basic accommodation.

name: Shri Nakoda Parshwanath
shortDescription: One of the most revered Jain temples in Rajasthan, famous for the miraculous idol of Parshwanath and Bhairav Dev.
description: Shri Nakoda Parshwanath Temple, near Balotra in Barmer district, Rajasthan, is one of the most important and revered Jain pilgrimage sites. The temple houses the miraculous Moolnayak idol of Shri Parshwanath and is famous for the protective deity Shri Nakoda Bhairav (also known as Bhairav Dev). The temple was originally built centuries ago and has been renovated multiple times. Devotees believe that prayers to Nakoda Bhairav grant protection and remove obstacles. The temple attracts millions of pilgrims annually, making it one of the busiest Jain temples in India.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Jodhpur (130 km). Nearest railway station: Balotra (10 km). Regular buses from Jodhpur and Ahmedabad.
dharamshalaInfo: Large dharamshala complex near the temple with hundreds of rooms, bhojanshala, and parking.

name: Shri Kesariyaji (Rishabhdev)
shortDescription: An ancient and highly revered temple of Adinath near Udaipur, known for the kesariyaji (saffron-colored) idol.
description: Shri Kesariyaji, also known as Rishabhdev or Dhulev, is one of the most revered Digambara Jain temples located near Udaipur in the Udaipur district of Rajasthan. The temple houses an ancient black idol of Adinath (Rishabhadeva) that is worshipped with kesar (saffron), hence the name Kesariyaji. The temple is believed to be over 2,500 years old and holds immense spiritual significance. It also attracts Hindu devotees who worship the deity as Kesariya Dev. The annual Dhwaja Mahotsav is a grand celebration.
highlights: Ancient Adinath idol worshipped with kesar (saffron)
Believed to be over 2,500 years old
Revered by both Jains and Hindus
howToReach: Nearest airport: Udaipur (64 km). Nearest railway station: Rishabhdev (1 km). Well connected by road from Udaipur.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala managed by Shri Digambar Jain Trust with rooms and bhojan facilities.

name: Shri Osian Jain Temples
shortDescription: Ancient 8th–11th century Jain temples in the Thar desert, showcasing the finest Pratihara temple architecture.
description: The Osian Jain Temples are located in Osian town, about 65 km from Jodhpur in Rajasthan. Dating from the 8th to 11th century, these temples are masterpieces of the Pratihara dynasty's architectural style. The Mahavira Temple is the most prominent, featuring intricate carvings on its torana (gateway) and mandapa (hall). The temple town was once a major center of Jain faith in the Thar desert. The temples feature beautifully sculpted panels depicting Jain Tirthankaras, celestial beings, and decorative motifs. The desert setting adds a unique charm.
highlights: Ancient Jain center in Thar desert
howToReach: Nearest airport: Jodhpur (65 km). Nearest railway station: Osian (1 km). Regular buses from Jodhpur.

name: Shri Lodhurva (Lodurva) Jain Temple
shortDescription: A beautifully carved desert temple near Jaisalmer, dedicated to Parshwanath, with a legendary Kamadhenu tree.
description: Shri Lodhurva Jain Temple is located about 15 km northwest of Jaisalmer in Rajasthan. The temple is dedicated to Shri Parshwanath, the 23rd Tirthankara. Lodhurva was the ancient capital of the Bhati Rajputs before Jaisalmer was founded. The temple is famous for its beautiful sandstone carvings and the legendary Kalpavriksha (wish-fulfilling tree) inside the complex. The ornate torana (arched gateway) of the temple is considered one of the finest examples of desert temple architecture.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Jaisalmer (18 km). Nearest railway station: Jaisalmer (15 km). Cabs and auto-rickshaws from Jaisalmer.

name: Jaisalmer Jain Temples
shortDescription: Exquisite 12th–15th century Jain temples inside Jaisalmer Fort, famed for their delicate yellow sandstone carvings.
description: The Jaisalmer Jain Temples are a group of seven beautifully carved Jain temples located within the Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Qila). Built between the 12th and 15th centuries, these temples are dedicated to various Tirthankaras including Rishabhadeva, Sambhavanath, and Parshwanath. The temples feature incredibly delicate yellow sandstone carvings that glow golden in the desert sun. The Chandraprabhu Temple and Parshwanath Temple are the most ornate. The complex also houses an ancient library (Gyan Bhandar) with rare Jain manuscripts dating back to the 11th century.
highlights: Ancient Gyan Bhandar library with rare manuscripts
UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of fort)
howToReach: Inside Jaisalmer Fort. Nearest airport: Jaisalmer (5 km). Nearest railway station: Jaisalmer (2 km). Walkable within the fort.

name: Shri Adinath Digambar Jain Mandir, Ahar
nameHindi: श्री आदिनाथ दिगंबर जैन मंदिर, आहड़
shortDescription: An ancient Digambara Jain temple complex in Ahar (Udaipur) with historical importance dating back several centuries.
description: The Shri Adinath Digambar Jain Mandir in Ahar, a suburb of Udaipur in Rajasthan, is an important Jain pilgrimage site. Ahar (ancient Aghata) has a rich historical legacy and was an important center for Jainism. The temple complex features ancient idols of Adinath and other Tirthankaras. The main temple houses a revered idol of Shri Adinath made of black stone. The complex also includes the famous Ahar cenotaphs (Mahasati) of the Mewar rulers nearby, adding to the cultural significance of the area.
highlights: Near Ahar cenotaphs of Mewar rulers
howToReach: Located in Udaipur city. Nearest airport: Udaipur (25 km). Nearest railway station: Udaipur City (3 km). Auto-rickshaws and cabs available.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain dharamshala near the temple with basic rooms.

name: Khajuraho Jain Temples
shortDescription: Stunning 10th–11th century Chandela-era Jain temples, part of the UNESCO World Heritage Khajuraho complex.
description: The Jain Temples of Khajuraho in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh, form the eastern group of the famous Khajuraho temple complex. Built during the Chandela dynasty (10th–11th century), these temples are dedicated to Jain Tirthankaras including Adinath, Parshwanath, and Shantinath. The Parshwanath Temple is the largest and most ornate of the Jain group, featuring exquisite sculptural work. The Adinath Temple and Ghantai Temple are also notable. These temples are part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site and showcase the religious harmony of the Chandela period.
highlights: Parshwanath Temple — most ornate Jain temple
howToReach: Nearest airport: Khajuraho (3 km). Nearest railway station: Khajuraho (6 km). Flights from Delhi and Varanasi.

name: Shri Bawangaja
shortDescription: Home to India's tallest Jain rock-cut idol — a 84-foot monolithic statue of Lord Adinath carved into a cliff.
description: Shri Bawangaja is a prominent Digambara Jain pilgrimage located in Barwani district, Madhya Pradesh. The highlight is the massive 84-foot (52 gaj = bawan gaj, hence the name) rock-cut idol of Shri Adinath (Rishabhadeva) carved into the hillside. It is one of the tallest Jain idols in the world. The site also features numerous smaller temples and caves on the hill. The annual Mahamastakabhisheka attracts thousands of devotees. The natural setting amidst the Satpura hills adds to the spiritual ambiance.
highlights: One of tallest Jain idols in the world
howToReach: Nearest airport: Indore (150 km). Nearest railway station: Barwani (8 km). Buses from Indore and Barwani.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala at the base of the hill managed by Digambar Jain Samiti.

name: Shri Muktagiri
shortDescription: A scenic hillside pilgrimage with 52 Jain temples, waterfalls, and a beautiful natural setting at the MP-Maharashtra border.
description: Shri Muktagiri is a famous Digambara Jain Siddhakshetra located on the Madhya Pradesh-Maharashtra border (Betul district, MP). The site features 52 beautifully carved Jain temples spread across a lush green hillside with natural waterfalls. The main temple houses an idol of Shri Parshwanath. It is believed that many Jain monks attained Moksha (Mukti) here, giving the place its name. The scenic waterfalls during the monsoon season add to its charm. The combination of natural beauty and spiritual sanctity makes it a unique pilgrimage.
bestTimeToVisit: October to February (waterfalls in monsoon July-Sept)
howToReach: Nearest airport: Nagpur (180 km). Nearest railway station: Paratwada (40 km). Buses from Amravati and Betul.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain Dharamshala near the temple complex with rooms and bhojanshala.

name: Shri Kundalpur (Damoh)
shortDescription: A major Digambara Jain pilgrimage near Damoh, Madhya Pradesh, with 63 temples and the Bade Baba temple atop a hill.
description: Shri Kundalpur near Damoh in Madhya Pradesh is one of the most important Digambara Jain pilgrimage centers. The site has 63 Jain temples, with the Bade Baba ka Mandir (dedicated to Adinath) being the main temple atop the hill. Kundalpur is believed to be the place where Lord Mahavira spent his 12th Chaturmas (monsoon retreat). The site features the Dashrath Ka Mahal and several ancient structures. The peaceful atmosphere and hilltop setting make it ideal for spiritual contemplation. Major gatherings occur during Panchkalyanak celebrations.
highlights: Bade Baba ka Mandir atop hill
howToReach: Nearest airport: Jabalpur (120 km). Nearest railway station: Damoh (15 km). Buses and taxis from Damoh.
dharamshalaInfo: Multiple dharamshalas in the complex managed by Digambar Jain Atishay Kshetra Committee.

name: Ellora Jain Caves
shortDescription: Stunning 9th–10th century rock-cut Jain caves (Caves 30–34) at the UNESCO World Heritage Ellora complex.
description: The Jain caves at Ellora (Caves 30 to 34) in Aurangabad, Maharashtra, are magnificent rock-cut structures dating from the 9th–10th century. Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Ellora Caves complex, these five Jain caves feature exquisite carvings of Tirthankaras, yaksha-yakshini figures, and elaborate lotus ceiling patterns. The Indra Sabha (Cave 32) is the most impressive, a two-story cave with a monolithic elephant and intricate paintings. The Jagannath Sabha (Cave 33) and Chhota Kailash (Cave 30) are also remarkable. These caves showcase the artistic brilliance of Jain artisans of the Rashtrakuta period.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Aurangabad (30 km). Nearest railway station: Aurangabad (29 km). Regular buses and taxis from Aurangabad.

name: Shri Mangi Tungi
shortDescription: Twin peaks with ancient Jain temples and the world's tallest Jain statue (108 ft) of Lord Rishabhadeva.
description: Shri Mangi Tungi is a sacred Jain Siddhakshetra located in Nashik district, Maharashtra. The twin peaks of Mangi and Tungi rise to about 4,343 feet and feature ancient Jain caves and temples carved into the rock. It is believed that 99.5 crore (almost one billion) Jain monks attained Moksha here. In 2016, the world's tallest Jain statue — a 108-foot idol of Lord Rishabhadeva (Adinath) — was installed at the base. The climb to the peaks involves approximately 4,000 steps through stunning natural terrain. The site holds immense spiritual significance for Digambara Jains.
highlights: Almost one billion monks attained Moksha here
howToReach: Nearest airport: Nashik (125 km). Nearest railway station: Manmad (60 km). Buses from Nashik and Manmad.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala at the base with accommodation and bhojanshala managed by Mangi Tungi Trust.

name: Shri Antriksh Parshwanath
shortDescription: A miraculous temple where the idol of Parshwanath is believed to float in mid-air without any support.
description: Shri Antriksh Parshwanath Temple is located in Shirpur (Shironj) in Budhni tehsil, Sehore district, Madhya Pradesh. The temple is famous for its miraculous Moolnayak idol of Shri Parshwanath, the 23rd Tirthankara, which is believed to hang/float in mid-air without any physical support — hence the name 'Antriksh' (meaning 'space/sky'). The idol appears to be suspended between the floor and ceiling. This phenomenon has made it one of the most visited Atishaya Kshetras (places of miracles) in Jainism. The temple draws curious visitors and devout pilgrims alike.
highlights: Idol believed to float in mid-air
One of most visited miracle temples
Draws both pilgrims and curious visitors
howToReach: Nearest airport: Bhopal (90 km). Nearest railway station: Budhni (5 km). Buses from Bhopal and Sehore.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala near the temple with basic rooms for pilgrims.

name: Shri Moodabidri (1000 Pillar Temple)
shortDescription: Known as the 'Jain Kashi', home to the famous Saavira Kambada Basadi (1000 Pillar Temple) built in the 15th century.
description: Moodabidri (also Moodbidri) in Dakshina Kannada district, Karnataka, is known as 'Jain Kashi' due to its concentration of 18 Jain basadis (temples). The most famous is the Saavira Kambada Basadi (Thousand Pillar Temple), also known as Tribhuvana Tilaka Chudamani Basadi, built in 1430 CE. No two of its 1,000 pillars are alike — each features unique carvings. The temple is dedicated to Lord Chandranatha (8th Tirthankara). Moodabidri was a major center of Jain learning and culture for centuries, and the town retains its old-world Jain charm.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Mangaluru (35 km). Nearest railway station: Mangaluru (38 km). Regular buses from Mangaluru.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain matha and dharamshala available near the temples.

name: Shri Karkala Gomateshwara
shortDescription: A 42-foot monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali (Gommateshwara) on a hilltop, the second tallest of its kind.
description: Karkala in Udupi district, Karnataka, is home to a magnificent 42-foot (12.8 m) monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali (Gommateshwara) installed in 1432 CE. Standing atop a rocky hill, it is the second tallest Bahubali statue after Shravanabelagola. The Mahamastakabhisheka ceremony is performed here every 12 years. Karkala is also known for its numerous Jain basadis including the Chaturmukha Basadi (four-faced temple). The town has been a significant Jain center since the medieval period under the Bhairarasa Wodeyar rulers.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Mangaluru (50 km). Nearest railway station: Mangaluru (52 km). Regular buses from Mangaluru and Udupi.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain dharamshala available near the Gomateshwara hill.

name: Shri Venur Gomateshwara
shortDescription: A 38-foot monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali in coastal Karnataka, the third tallest of its kind.
description: Venur in Dakshina Kannada district, Karnataka, houses a 38-foot (11.5 m) monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali (Gommateshwara), installed in 1604 CE by Thimmanna Ajila. It is the third tallest Bahubali statue in India after Shravanabelagola and Karkala. The statue stands in a serene setting near the Gurupur river. The Mahamastakabhisheka is performed every 12 years. Venur also has other notable Jain basadis and is part of the rich Jain heritage belt of coastal Karnataka.
highlights: Part of coastal Karnataka Jain belt
howToReach: Nearest airport: Mangaluru (50 km). Nearest railway station: Mangaluru (55 km). Buses from Mangaluru.

name: Shri Humcha (Hombuja)
shortDescription: An ancient Digambara Jain center with the revered Padmavati Devi temple and 2000+ year history.
description: Humcha (Hombuja) in Shimoga district, Karnataka, is one of the oldest and most important Digambara Jain centers in South India, with a history of over 2,000 years. The town is renowned for the Shri Padmavati Devi temple (a Jain protective goddess) which attracts devotees from across India. The Humcha Jain Math has been a center of Jain learning and religious leadership for centuries. The annual Rathotsav and Laksha Deepotsav festivals are major celebrations. The area features multiple ancient basadis and inscriptions dating back to the Kadamba and Hoysala periods.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Hubli (100 km). Nearest railway station: Shimoga (60 km). Buses from Shimoga and Hubli.
dharamshalaInfo: Accommodation available at Humcha Jain Math for pilgrims.

name: Shri Kulpakji (Kolanupaka)
shortDescription: An ancient Jain pilgrimage in Telangana with a 2000+ year old idol — one of the oldest Jain sites in South India.
description: Shri Kulpakji (Kolanupaka) in Nalgonda district, Telangana, is one of the most ancient Jain pilgrimage sites in South India, with a history spanning over 2,000 years. The temple houses a revered idol of Lord Rishabhadeva (Adinath) made of jade (Marakata) stone, believed to be one of the oldest Jain idols in existence. The site has been patronized by multiple dynasties including the Satavahanas, Chalukyas, and Kakatiyas. Both Shvetambara and Digambara communities maintain temples here. The town also has historical connections to the Kakatiya dynasty.
highlights: 2000+ year old jade idol of Rishabhadeva
One of oldest Jain sites in South India
howToReach: Nearest airport: Hyderabad (80 km). Nearest railway station: Alair (15 km). Buses from Hyderabad.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain dharamshala managed by both Shvetambara and Digambara Jain trusts.

name: Shri Tirumalai Jain Complex
shortDescription: A historic Jain pilgrimage in Tamil Nadu with a 56-foot Neminath statue and ancient rock-cut temples.
description: Shri Tirumalai is an important Digambara Jain pilgrimage site located near Polur in Tiruvannamalai district, Tamil Nadu. The complex features a 56-foot (17m) statue of Lord Neminath carved from a single rock, one of the tallest in South India. The site includes ancient rock-cut Jain caves, the Adinath and Neminath temples, and inscriptions from the Pallava and Chola periods. Surrounded by lush green hills, it provides a serene atmosphere for pilgrimage. Tirumalai was an important center of Jain faith in the Tamil region for over a millennium.
highlights: Ancient Pallava and Chola era inscriptions
howToReach: Nearest airport: Chennai (190 km). Nearest railway station: Polur (18 km). Buses from Tiruvannamalai and Chennai.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain dharamshala at the base of the hill for pilgrims.

name: Shri Rajgir Jain Temples
shortDescription: Sacred hills of Rajgir where Lord Mahavira spent 14 rainy seasons — with Vipulachal and Sonbhandar caves.
description: Rajgir in Nalanda district, Bihar, holds immense significance for Jains as Lord Mahavira spent 14 Chaturmas (rainy season retreats) here. The ancient capital of Magadha, Rajgir features several important Jain sites including the Vipulachal hill temples, Sonbhandar caves, and the Jal Mandir at Griddhakuta. The Shri Digambar Jain temple on Vipulachal hill houses ancient idols. The town is sacred to both Jains and Buddhists. The hot springs (Brahmakund) and surrounding five hills (Panch Pahadi) add to its spiritual atmosphere. A ropeway connects to the hilltop temples.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Patna (100 km). Nearest railway station: Rajgir (1 km). Regular buses from Patna and Nalanda.
dharamshalaInfo: Multiple Jain dharamshalas in Rajgir town for pilgrims visiting Vipulachal and surrounding sites.

name: Shri Vaishali Jain Shrine
shortDescription: The birthplace of Lord Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara — an ancient and deeply sacred Jain pilgrimage.
description: Vaishali in Vaishali district, Bihar, is one of the most sacred Jain pilgrimage sites as it is the birthplace of Lord Mahavira (according to Shvetambara tradition). The ancient city was the capital of the Licchavi republic, one of the world's earliest republics. The Shri Mahavirji temple marks the birthplace. Vaishali is also associated with the 24th Tirthankara's early life before he renounced the world. The site features ancient ruins, an Ashokan pillar, and archaeological remains of the great city. The area has been declared an archaeological heritage zone.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Patna (55 km). Nearest railway station: Hajipur (35 km). Buses from Patna and Hajipur.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain dharamshala near the main temple for pilgrims.

name: Shri Champapuri
shortDescription: The ancient capital of Anga kingdom where the 12th Tirthankara Vasupujya attained Moksha.
description: Champapuri (modern-day Bhagalpur area) in Bihar is a revered Jain Siddhakshetra. It was the ancient capital of the Anga Mahajanapada and is associated with the 12th Tirthankara, Shri Vasupujya, who is believed to have attained Nirvana here. The site features the main temple dedicated to Lord Vasupujya along with several other Jain shrines. Champapuri has been mentioned extensively in ancient Jain literature and Puranas. Despite being lesser-known than some larger pilgrimages, it is revered for its Tirthankara association.
highlights: Mentioned in Jain literature and Puranas
Multiple Jain shrines in the area
howToReach: Nearest airport: Patna (200 km). Nearest railway station: Bhagalpur (5 km). Regular trains from Patna and Kolkata.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain dharamshala available near the main temple.

name: Shri Hastinapur Jain Tirth
shortDescription: An ancient Jain pilgrimage in UP — birthplace of three Tirthankaras and the legendary Mahabharata capital.
description: Hastinapur in Meerut district, Uttar Pradesh, is one of the most significant Jain pilgrimage sites. It is believed to be the birthplace of three Tirthankaras — Shri Shantinath (16th), Shri Kunthunath (17th), and Shri Arahnath (18th). The ancient city is also famous as the capital of the Kuru dynasty from the Mahabharata. The Shri Digambar Jain Mandir complex features the grand Jambudweep — a stunning architectural model depicting Jain cosmology. The Ashtapad Tirth, Kailash Parvat replica, and the Shvetambara Jain temples are also major attractions. The town is a living center of Jain scholarship and devotion.
highlights: Ashtapad Tirth and Kailash Parvat replica
howToReach: Nearest airport: Delhi (120 km). Nearest railway station: Meerut (37 km). Buses from Delhi and Meerut.
dharamshalaInfo: Multiple dharamshalas in the temple complex managed by both Digambar and Shvetambar trusts.

name: Shri Ayodhya Jain Temples
shortDescription: The birthplace of the first Tirthankara Lord Rishabhadeva (Adinath) and four other Tirthankaras.
description: Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh is one of the most sacred cities for Jains as it is the birthplace of five Tirthankaras — Shri Rishabhadeva (1st), Shri Ajitanath (2nd), Shri Abhinandannath (4th), Shri Sumatinath (5th), and Shri Anantanath (14th). The main Jain temples include the Shri Digambar Jain Mandir at the Tirthankara birth sites and the Shvetambara temples. The ancient city holds profound Jain significance as it was the capital of King Nabhi and Queen Marudevi, parents of Lord Rishabhadeva. The city has been a center of Jain pilgrimage for millennia.
highlights: Capital of King Nabhi — father of Adinath
Ancient city of immense Jain significance
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ayodhya (7 km) / Lucknow (130 km). Nearest railway station: Ayodhya Junction (1 km). Trains from Delhi, Lucknow, Varanasi.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain dharamshalas available near the main temples managed by local Jain sangh.

name: Shri Kaushambi Jain Tirth
shortDescription: An ancient pilgrimage near Prayagraj where several Tirthankaras preached — rich in archaeological heritage.
description: Kaushambi in Uttar Pradesh is an important Jain pilgrimage site of great antiquity. The ancient city of Kaushambi was a major center of Jain activity where several Tirthankaras, including Lord Mahavira, preached their sermons. The archaeological site features ancient ruins, inscriptions, and the remains of Jain viharas (monasteries). The Shri Digambar Jain temple preserves the ancient Jain heritage of the site. Kaushambi was the capital of the Vatsa kingdom and has yielded important Jain sculptures and artifacts now housed in various museums.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Prayagraj (55 km). Nearest railway station: Bharwari (12 km). Buses from Prayagraj.

name: Shri Digambar Jain Lal Mandir
shortDescription: The oldest and most famous Jain temple in Delhi, built in the 16th century opposite the Red Fort.
description: Shri Digambar Jain Lal Mandir (Red Temple) is the oldest and most famous Jain temple in Delhi, located directly opposite the Red Fort on Chandni Chowk. Originally built in 1526 during the reign of Emperor Shah Jahan, the temple has been renovated several times. It is dedicated to Lord Mahavira and also houses idols of Adinath and other Tirthankaras. The temple is known for its beautiful red sandstone architecture and the famous Jain Bird Hospital (Charity Birds Hospital) attached to it, which treats thousands of injured birds — embodying the Jain principle of Ahimsa (non-violence).
highlights: Oldest Jain temple in Delhi (1526 CE)
Famous Jain Bird Hospital (Ahimsa in action)
howToReach: Nearest metro: Chandni Chowk (Delhi Metro Red Line). Close to Old Delhi Railway Station. Easily accessible by auto and cab.
dharamshalaInfo: Jain dharamshala attached to the temple complex for pilgrims.

name: Shri Madhuban
shortDescription: The base town for Sammed Shikharji pilgrimage with grand Jain temples, dharamshalas, and a vibrant Jain community.
description: Madhuban is the base town for the Sammed Shikharji pilgrimage in Giridih district, Jharkhand. While Sammed Shikharji atop Parasnath Hill is the main pilgrimage, Madhuban itself is a thriving Jain center with numerous grand temples, dharamshalas, and bhojanshala facilities. The town has the Shri Parshwanath temple and several other beautiful shrines. Most pilgrims stay in Madhuban before and after the Sammed Shikharji trek. The town has a vibrant Jain community and hosts major religious conferences and events throughout the year.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ranchi (180 km). Nearest railway station: Parasnath (10 km). Buses from Ranchi, Kolkata, and Patna.
dharamshalaInfo: Dozens of dharamshalas run by various Jain trusts with hundreds of rooms, bhojanshala, and modern amenities.

name: Shri Nainagiri Jain Tirth
shortDescription: A revered hilltop Digambara Jain pilgrimage in Chhattisgarh with ancient temples and a striking colossus.
description: Shri Nainagiri (also known as Nainagiri Tirth) is an important Digambara Jain pilgrimage located in Rajnandgaon district, Chhattisgarh. The site features Jain temples atop a hill with ancient idols of Tirthankaras including a striking large idol of Adinath. The hill offers panoramic views of the surrounding plains. Nainagiri has been mentioned in ancient Jain texts and is considered a Siddhakshetra. The peaceful hilltop environment and the historical significance make it a cherished destination for Jain pilgrims visiting central India.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Raipur (130 km). Nearest railway station: Rajnandgaon (20 km). Buses from Raipur and Rajnandgaon.
dharamshalaInfo: Basic dharamshala available at the base for pilgrims.

name: Shri Chandraprabhu Temple, Tijara
shortDescription: A grand Digambara Jain temple complex near Alwar with stunning architecture and a massive temple hall.
description: The Shri Chandraprabhu Digambar Jain Atishay Kshetra at Tijara in Alwar district, Rajasthan, is one of the most impressive Jain temple complexes in North India. The main temple dedicated to Lord Chandraprabhu (8th Tirthankara) is a grand structure with a massive prayer hall that can accommodate thousands. The temple features exquisite marble work, painted ceilings, and imposing spires. The complex includes gardens, a museum, and bhojanshala. Tijara attracts large numbers of devotees, especially during Panchkalyanak and Dashlakshan Parva celebrations.
highlights: Exquisite marble work and painted ceilings
howToReach: Nearest airport: Delhi (130 km). Nearest railway station: Tijara (2 km). Buses from Alwar and Delhi.
dharamshalaInfo: Large dharamshala complex with modern rooms, AC/non-AC, and Jain bhojanshala.

name: Shri Padampura Jain Temple
shortDescription: A beautiful Digambara Jain temple near Jaipur known for its intricate marble work and peaceful campus.
description: Shri Padampura Digambar Jain Atishay Kshetra is located near Jaipur in Rajasthan. The temple complex is dedicated to Lord Padmaprabhu (6th Tirthankara) and is known for its pristine white marble architecture and intricate carvings. The campus includes a beautiful garden, dharamshala, and bhojanshala. The temple features a serene prayer hall with detailed ceiling artwork. It is a popular spiritual retreat for Jain families in the Jaipur region and hosts regular religious discourse and pravachan sessions.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Jaipur (15 km). Nearest railway station: Jaipur Junction (12 km). Auto-rickshaws and cabs from Jaipur.
dharamshalaInfo: Dharamshala on campus with rooms and Jain bhojanshala.

name: Shri Sarnath Jain Temple
shortDescription: A significant Jain temple at Sarnath where Shri Shreyansnath, the 11th Tirthankara, is said to have been born.
description: Sarnath near Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, is significant for Jains as the birthplace of Shri Shreyansnath (Shreyanasanath), the 11th Tirthankara. While Sarnath is more widely known as a Buddhist site, the Jain temple here commemorates this important Tirthankara connection. The Digambar Jain temple features a beautiful idol of Lord Shreyansnath. The archaeological site also contains Jain artifacts and inscriptions from various periods. The temple is a peaceful oasis amidst the rich multi-faith heritage of the Sarnath-Varanasi region.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Varanasi (28 km). Nearest railway station: Varanasi Junction (10 km). Auto-rickshaws and cabs from Varanasi.

name: Shri Parshwanath Temple, Kolkata
shortDescription: A stunning Shvetambara Jain temple in Kolkata, renowned for its dazzling glass mosaic, mirror work, and ornate interiors.
description: The Shri Parshwanath Jain Temple (also known as Calcutta Jain Temple) is located in the Badridas Temple Street area of Kolkata, West Bengal. Built in 1867, this Shvetambara temple is dedicated to Shri Parshwanath but also houses idols of Sheetalnath and Chandraprabhu. The temple is a visual feast with its dazzling glass mosaic work, ornate mirror decorations, intricate floral designs, and gilded interiors. The complex includes beautiful gardens with European-style fountains and sculptures. It is considered one of the most beautiful Jain temples in Eastern India.
location: Badridas Temple Street, Kolkata, West Bengal
highlights: Dazzling glass mosaic and mirror work
Most beautiful Jain temple in East India
howToReach: Located in central Kolkata. Nearest metro: Burrabazar. Nearest railway station: Howrah (4 km). Cabs and autos available.

name: Shri Jain Shwetambar Dharamshala, Palitana
shortDescription: One of the largest Jain dharamshala complexes at the base of Shatrunjaya, serving lakhs of pilgrims annually.
description: The Shri Jain Shwetambar Dharamshala complex at Palitana is one of the largest and most well-organized Jain pilgrim accommodation facilities in India. Located at the base (Taleti) of Shatrunjaya Hill, multiple dharamshalas are managed by various Jain trusts and sanghatan. They offer clean rooms (both AC and non-AC), pure Jain vegetarian bhojanshala (dining), hot water, locker facilities, and parking. The complex serves lakhs of pilgrims who visit Palitana annually for the Shatrunjaya yatra. Notable dharamshalas include those managed by Anandji Kalyanji Trust, Seth Motisha Trust, and various city-based Jain Sangh organizations.
highlights: One of the largest Jain dharamshala complexes
Managed by Anandji Kalyanji & other trusts
howToReach: Located at Palitana Taleti. Nearest airport: Bhavnagar (50 km). Nearest railway station: Palitana (3 km). Auto and rickshaws from station.
dharamshalaInfo: This IS one of the dharamshala complexes. Advance booking recommended during peak season (Nov-Feb).

name: Shri Jain Dharamshala, Madhuban (Sammed Shikharji)
shortDescription: Large dharamshala complex at Madhuban serving pilgrims of Sammed Shikharji — the supreme Jain pilgrimage.
description: The Jain Dharamshala complex at Madhuban serves as the primary accommodation hub for pilgrims undertaking the Sammed Shikharji yatra. Managed by multiple Jain trusts including Bhagwan Shri Parshwanath Dharamshala, Shri Shikharji Tirth Kshetra Committee, and various sangh-managed facilities, this complex offers hundreds of rooms ranging from dormitory-style to premium accommodation. Facilities include bhojanshala serving fresh Jain satvic food, medical aid, cloakroom, hot water, and trek gear rental. The complex buzzes with activity during the pilgrimage season from October to March.
highlights: Primary accommodation for Sammed Shikharji pilgrims
Hundreds of rooms in multiple dharamshalas
Medical aid and trek gear rental
Managed by multiple revered Jain trusts
howToReach: Nearest airport: Ranchi (180 km). Nearest railway station: Parasnath (10 km). Buses from station to Madhuban.
dharamshalaInfo: This IS the dharamshala complex. Book via trust offices or local agents during peak season.

name: Shri Jain Dharamshala, Haridwar
shortDescription: A well-known Jain dharamshala in the holy city of Haridwar, serving Jain pilgrims and travelers.
description: The Shri Jain Dharamshala in Haridwar, Uttarakhand, is a well-known accommodation facility for Jain pilgrims and travelers visiting the holy city. Located conveniently near the main ghats, it provides clean rooms and a pure Jain vegetarian bhojanshala. Haridwar, though primarily a Hindu pilgrimage city, has a significant Jain presence and the dharamshala ensures Jain travelers have access to faith-appropriate accommodation and satvik food. The facility is particularly popular among Jain families who combine their spiritual journey with visits to Rishikesh and the Himalayan foothills.
highlights: Serves Jain travelers in holy city
bestTimeToVisit: March to June, September to November
howToReach: Nearest airport: Dehradun (35 km). Nearest railway station: Haridwar Junction (2 km). Auto-rickshaws from station.
dharamshalaInfo: This IS a Jain dharamshala. Contact: Local Haridwar Jain Samaj for booking.

name: Shri Jain Dharamshala, Ujjain
shortDescription: A Jain dharamshala in the ancient city of Ujjain, serving pilgrims visiting the local Jain temples.
description: The Shri Jain Dharamshala in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh, accommodates Jain pilgrims visiting this ancient city. Ujjain has several notable Jain temples including the Shri Parshwanath Digambar Jain Mandir in the old city and the Siddhavat Jain Tirth near the river. The dharamshala provides clean rooms, Jain bhojanshala, and a peaceful environment. Ujjain, one of the seven sacred cities of India and the site of the famous Kumbh Mela, has a Jain heritage dating back to the Maurya period. Avantika (ancient Ujjain) is mentioned in several Jain texts.
highlights: Accommodation for Ujjain Jain temple visitors
Jain heritage dating to Maurya period
howToReach: Nearest airport: Indore (55 km). Nearest railway station: Ujjain Junction (2 km). Auto-rickshaws from station.
dharamshalaInfo: This IS a Jain dharamshala. Contact: Ujjain Jain Samaj for booking.

name: Shri Jain Dharamshala, Ajmer
shortDescription: A long-established Jain dharamshala in Ajmer serving pilgrims visiting Ajmer and nearby Jain temples.
description: The Shri Jain Dharamshala in Ajmer, Rajasthan, is a well-established pilgrim accommodation facility. Ajmer has several Jain temples including the Shri Nasiyan Jain Temple (also known as the Red Temple or Soni Ji Ki Nasiyan) which features a stunning gold-plated hall (Swarna Nagari) depicting Jain cosmology. The dharamshala serves Jain pilgrims and travelers visiting these temples and nearby sacred sites like Pushkar. Clean rooms, Jain bhojanshala, and parking facilities are available. Ajmer's Nasiyan temple is one of the most visually stunning Jain temples in India.
highlights: Near the famous Nasiyan Jain Temple (Red Temple)
howToReach: Nearest airport: Jaipur (135 km). Nearest railway station: Ajmer Junction (2 km). Auto-rickshaws from station.
dharamshalaInfo: This IS a Jain dharamshala. Multiple dharamshalas in Ajmer managed by various Jain sangh.

name: Shri Nasiyan (Soni Ji Ki Nasiyan), Ajmer
nameHindi: श्री नसियां (सोनी जी की नसियां), अजमेर
shortDescription: The 'Red Temple' of Ajmer with its breathtaking gold-plated Swarna Nagari hall depicting Jain cosmology.
description: Shri Nasiyan, popularly known as Soni Ji Ki Nasiyan or the Red Temple, is a Digambara Jain temple in Ajmer, Rajasthan. Built in 1865, its main attraction is the Swarna Nagari (City of Gold) — a breathtaking hall on the first floor featuring gold-plated wooden figures depicting scenes from Jain scriptures, including the story of Lord Rishabhadeva. The hall took 20 years to create and uses an estimated 1,000 kg of gold. The red sandstone exterior gives it the name 'Red Temple'. The temple is dedicated to Shri Adinath and is considered one of the most aesthetically magnificent Jain temples in India.
highlights: Swarna Nagari — gold-plated hall (1,000 kg gold)
Depicts Jain scripture scenes in gold
One of India's most magnificent Jain temples
howToReach: In Ajmer city center. Nearest airport: Jaipur (135 km). Nearest railway station: Ajmer Junction (1 km). Auto-rickshaws and cabs available.

name: Gwalior Fort Jain Sculptures
shortDescription: Magnificent rock-cut Jain colossi on the walls of Gwalior Fort — among the finest medieval Jain sculptures in India.
description: The Gwalior Fort in Madhya Pradesh features a spectacular collection of rock-cut Jain sculptures carved into the cliff faces along the approach road. Known as the Siddhachal Jain Caves, these 7th–15th century carvings include colossal images of Tirthankaras ranging from 6 to 57 feet tall. The sculptures depict Adinath, Parshwanath, and other Tirthankaras in standing (kayotsarga) and seated (padmasana) postures. The largest is a 57-foot standing image of Adinath. These masterpieces survived Muslim invasions that damaged many others. They are among the finest medieval Jain monuments in central India.
highlights: Siddhachal Jain Caves on fort approach
howToReach: In Gwalior city. Nearest airport: Gwalior (10 km). Nearest railway station: Gwalior Junction (3 km). Auto and cabs available.

name: Shri Kunthalgiri
shortDescription: A scenic hilltop Digambara Jain Siddhakshetra in Maharashtra where many monks attained Moksha.
description: Shri Kunthalgiri is a revered Digambara Jain Siddhakshetra located in Nanded district, Maharashtra. Situated atop a hill, it is believed that many Jain monks attained Moksha (liberation) here. The main temple houses ancient idols of Tirthankaras, and the hilltop complex features multiple smaller shrines and meditation spaces. The site offers beautiful views of the surrounding landscape. Kunthalgiri is a peaceful and less-commercialized pilgrimage destination, making it ideal for devotees seeking quiet contemplation. The annual religious gatherings attract Jain devotees from across Maharashtra.
howToReach: Nearest airport: Nanded (30 km). Nearest railway station: Nanded (25 km). Buses and taxis from Nanded.
dharamshalaInfo: Basic dharamshala available for pilgrims.

name: Shri Sanganer Jain Temples
shortDescription: A cluster of ancient Jain temples in Sanganer near Jaipur, including the stunning Shri Adinath temple.
description: Sanganer, now a suburb of Jaipur in Rajasthan, is home to a beautiful cluster of ancient Jain temples. The most prominent is the Shri Adinath Jain Temple, featuring exquisite carvings and a grand shikhara (tower). The temples date back several centuries and showcase the Rajput-era Jain architectural style. Sanganer is famous both for its Jain temples and for its traditional block printing and handmade paper crafts. The temples are well-preserved and feature intricate torana (gateway) arches, carved pillars, and beautifully detailed ceiling panels.
highlights: Stunning Adinath temple with grand shikhara
howToReach: Located in Jaipur city. Nearest airport: Jaipur (3 km). Nearest railway station: Jaipur Junction (12 km). Auto-rickshaws available.

name: Shri Hathisingh Jain Temple
shortDescription: A prominent city temple in Ahmedabad known for elegant marble work and peaceful darshan atmosphere.
description: Shri Hathisingh Jain Temple in Ahmedabad is one of the best-known local Jain temples in Gujarat. Built in the 19th century and dedicated to Shri Dharmanath, it is admired for detailed carvings, ornate pillars, and traditional architecture. The temple is actively visited by local families for daily पूजा, pratikraman, and community gatherings.
howToReach: Located in Ahmedabad city. Easily reachable by local cab, metro, and auto-rickshaw.

name: Shri Chulgiri Digambar Jain Temple
shortDescription: A revered hill-facing local temple in Jaipur with a calm setting for darshan and meditation.
description: Shri Chulgiri Digambar Jain Temple, located on the outskirts of Jaipur, is a major local devotional center for the city Jain community. The temple complex is known for serene surroundings, elevated views, and regular spiritual activities. It serves as an accessible local pilgrimage point for residents and visitors.
highlights: Popular local Jain temple in Jaipur
howToReach: On Jaipur-Agra Road, reachable by private cab and city transport.

name: Shri Babu Amichand Panalal Adishwarji Jain Temple
nameHindi: श्री बाबू अमीचंद पानालाल आदिश्वरजी जैन मंदिर
shortDescription: A well-known Mumbai local Jain temple near Walkeshwar, visited daily by devotees.
description: This temple in Mumbai is an important local center of Jain devotion, known for its clean sanctum, regular rituals, and active participation from nearby families. It serves the daily spiritual needs of the local Jain community and remains one of the city’s frequently visited mandirs.
howToReach: Located in South Mumbai; reachable by taxi and local transport.

name: Shri Adinath Jain Temple, Wilson Garden
nameHindi: श्री आदिनाथ जैन मंदिर, विल्सन गार्डन
shortDescription: A prominent local Jain temple in Bengaluru serving daily city devotees.
description: Shri Adinath Jain Temple at Wilson Garden is among Bengaluru’s active local Jain temples. It hosts regular darshan, prarthana, and festival observances and is a central spiritual place for local Jain families in the area.
howToReach: Inside Wilson Garden, Bengaluru; well connected via BMTC buses and cabs.

name: Shri Kanch Mandir
shortDescription: A famous glass-work Jain temple in Indore and a key local spiritual landmark.
description: Kanch Mandir in Indore is a distinctive local Jain temple known for mirror and glass inlay work across interiors. Dedicated to Jain Tirthankaras, it is one of the most recognizable Jain landmarks in the city and is frequently visited by residents for daily and festive worship.
highlights: Located in old Indore market area
howToReach: In central Indore, reachable by local auto/cab from railway station and airport.

name: Shri Kamaldahji Digambar Jain Temple
shortDescription: A respected local Jain temple in Patna associated with old Jain heritage in Bihar.
description: Shri Kamaldahji Digambar Jain Temple in Patna is an important local center for Jain devotees. The temple is linked with the region’s deep Jain heritage and attracts regular local worshippers for daily rituals and special observances.
howToReach: Located in Patna city near Gulzarbagh area; reachable by cab and local transport.
